categories.name: Data Cleaning & Preparation
categories.judged_from: Notebook code, outputs and Markdown explanations
categories.limits: Judged from saved outputs. Student code is never run.

excellent.description: All relevant cleaning steps are performed and clearly justified. Missing values, data types, and inconsistencies are handled appropriately. Cleaning rationale is thoroughly explained in Markdown cells. Code runs without errors.

good.description: Most cleaning steps are performed correctly. Minor issues remain (e.g., one data type unconverted, incomplete explanation of a cleaning decision). Code runs with minimal warnings.

needs_work.description: Significant data quality issues are left unaddressed. Little or no explanation of cleaning decisions. Code contains errors that affect downstream analysis.

categories.name: Analysis & Visualizations
categories.judged_from: Notebook code, tables and the chart images saved in the notebook, checked against the assigned questions
categories.limits: Chart quality (titles, axes, legends) is judged from the saved images.

excellent.description: All questions from the assigned section are answered with appropriate tables or plots. Visualizations are well-chosen for the data, clearly labeled (titles, axes, legends), and easy to interpret. Analysis demonstrates strong command of course skills.

good.description: Most questions are answered correctly. Visualizations are generally appropriate but may have minor labeling issues or a less-than-optimal chart type choice. Analysis is mostly sound.

needs_work.description: Several questions are unanswered or answered incorrectly. Visualizations are missing, mislabeled, or inappropriate for the data. Analysis shows limited application of course skills.

categories.name: Interpretation & Written Summaries
categories.judged_from: Markdown cells next to each result

excellent.description: Every question includes a clear, thoughtful written summary that demonstrates understanding of what the results mean. Observations go beyond restating numbers and provide insight and context.

good.description: Most questions include written summaries. Interpretations are generally correct but may be surface-level or simply restate the output without deeper insight.

needs_work.description: Written summaries are missing for most questions or are too vague to demonstrate understanding. Little evidence that the student interpreted the results.

categories.name: Code Quality & Organization
categories.judged_from: Notebook structure, headings, comments, variable names, error outputs and cell execution order
categories.limits: 'Runs top to bottom' is judged from saved outputs and execution order, because student code is never run.

excellent.description: Notebook is well-organized with clear Markdown headings and logical flow. Code is clean, commented where needed, uses meaningful variable names, and runs top-to-bottom without errors. No leftover or unnecessary code.

good.description: Notebook is mostly organized. Code runs but may have minor issues: inconsistent formatting, sparse comments, or a few unused cells. Overall structure is followable.

needs_work.description: Notebook is disorganized or difficult to follow. Code does not run cleanly, has significant errors, or lacks structure. Headings and Markdown cells are missing or misused.

categories.name: Presentation of Findings
categories.judged_from: The transcript, plus the recording length for the time limit
categories.limits: The transcript has no speaker labels. Whether both partners presented is inferred from what is said (for example names and hand-offs) and must be confirmed by the professor.

excellent.description: Presentation is clear, well-organized, and stays within the time limit. Both partners participate in the delivery. Key findings are communicated effectively with references to visualizations. Presenters demonstrate strong understanding of their analysis.

good.description: Presentation covers the main findings and both partners participate, though delivery may be uneven. Some findings could be explained more clearly. Stays roughly within the time limit.

needs_work.description: Presentation is disorganized, significantly over or under time, or only one partner presents. Key findings are unclear or not supported by the analysis. Limited evidence of understanding.

categories.name: Collaboration & Formatting
categories.judged_from: Notebook header and file name (checked by code), plus responsibilities stated in the header
categories.limits: Whether both partners contributed meaningfully cannot be proven from the files. Flag it for the professor.

excellent.description: All submission guidelines are followed: header is complete, file is named correctly, partner and section responsibilities are clearly identified. Both partners contributed meaningfully.

good.description: Most guidelines are followed. Minor issues such as an incomplete header field or slightly incorrect filename. Both partners appear to have contributed.

needs_work.description: Multiple submission guidelines are not followed. Header is incomplete or missing. Filename does not follow the convention. Unclear whether both partners contributed.
